reviews.title: Customer Service Does Not Respond
reviews.text: I've been using Habitica for a couple of years now. Though it isn't the most attractive design, it works well for keeping task with daily routines. I like that it has the feel of old RPG's. The "Habits" functions have never worked well in terms of the frequency settings, but overall, everything else does what I need. I like supporting human creators. You can tell a lot of energy is invested in keeping it going. That said, I think I'll find another app because of the poor customer service. I have tried reaching out to Habitica recently with a question about one of the quests, and no one responded. Then I tried commenting with a question on Bluesky since someone from their team actively posts there. Again, no response. It doesn't sit well with me that they accept money from patrons but won't respond to email.

It also helps me with motivation and reminders for daily life activities (like remembering chores or self-care habits) and one-off tasks (like remembering to send an email or replace that light bulb that I always seem to forget). reviews.title: Pay to win
reviews.text:
It’s a great app and I definitely recommend it to anyone who is motivated by gamification. It’s a little confusing to navigate at first, but great once you get the hang of it. However if you want to collect all the pets and such, you have no choice but to subscribe. Pet quests can be gained if you join a party with people who have subscriptions, but for pets that can’t be obtained through quests you’re basically screwed. Challenges can give you gem rewards, but chances of winning are very slim. I would love if gems were purchasable with coins but were very expensive per gem to encourage people to either grind for them or subscribe. 
That being said I can see how that could be abused with FCV and spamming habits, so if that were implemented those things would need to be adjusted and capped. But I do think it’s doable and less scammy, and honestly a more motivating option. I’ve fallen off Habitica a lot because when those things are unattainable there’s little incentive to actually use the app
TL;DR: Good app overall but in my opinion the motivating factors are not sustainable. Claims not to be a pay to win game but absolutely is one if you want to collect things, which is the main reward system of the game. Needs adjustments

reviews.title: De-leveling
reviews.text:
How did the entire dev team think that stripping players of their LEVELS when dying to a boss was good idea?? I can get behind the party taking damage, losing gear/weapons, but it’s absurd to lose your LEVEL just because you died to the boss. There is no reason for this mechanic to exist. You punish EVERYONE because certain people can’t complete the dailies everyday. Again, it makes sense to lose your gear and take damage as a whole group, but to be de-leveled is where the mechanic is nonsense. This mechanic should be removed. Never have I played a game where I was stripped of my level status just because of losing to a boss.

Other than this, it’s fine.

reviews.title: Cross Platform Reminder Bug
reviews.text:
So far my experience has been mixed. Habitica doesn’t work as seamlessly as other to do solutions like Todoist, with  the biggest annoyance being broken cross platform reminder between PC, Android, and iOS. 

I’m using Habitica  for a very narrow purpose because I like the RPG mechanics. But I would not recommend this as anyone’s standalone approaching Light task management system. This bug has reportedly been open for years and has never been fixed.

reviews.title: Used for a Full Year
reviews.text:
This is hands-down the best goal app I’ve ever used. All the game stuff aside, the goal functions are entirely customizable and easy to use. Organization is clean. The hardest time of this last year was when I stopped using it for a few months, and I’ve recently started using it again religiously; I’m never going back. 

The game aspect is fun. It’s pretty sweet hitting goals and then seeing my dude in full moon-armor riding a purple dragon with a banner and a sword. Really though it’s just an incredibly solid goal app with a couple fun twists. 

My ONLY critique; I wish the quests weren’t so hard to do solo. I’m not exactly super social, and I’d love to fight monsters by myself. I’ve been on the same lunar quest for a few months now.

Get this app and DIVE into it. My life would be nowhere near as organized without it, and you can tell someone put their heart and soul into designing it.
